notes:
Speccify 0.11.1 organizes work around resources and prepares a lightweight Mac
to hand tasks to another Mac on the local network. This patch targets
**Mac Apple Silicon**. Windows stays at 0.11.0; its next planned release is 0.12.0.

## Refine plans and distinguish documents from models

- Edit a version's **Planning notes** after creating it. Keep refining the plan
  before cutting it into Specs; release notes describe what actually ships.
- **Docs** replaces Rules as the knowledge resource. Existing text UseCases
  become **Features** under Docs, preserving their identities, history and
  version relationships through a reviewed migration.
- **Models** contains graphical models. The former Domain type is called
  **UseCase** and starts with a flowchart editor without UI elements.
- Open a child model in a modal editor. Save the child explicitly, return to
  the parent and save that parent separately. The parent cannot be edited
  while its child editor is open.
- Return to the main project-opening window with the leftmost toolbar button.

## Arrange the resources you are using

Place document or collection tabs in a sidebar or either half of a split
Bottom area. Keep two Agent chats below the main editor and an editable Note
beside it. Existing documents keep their drafts and sessions; merely opening
or moving a resource starts no work. Busy work retains its placement safeguards.

Saved **Agents** are the entry for ordinary terminal work. Store a command and
arguments with the persona, including an explicit model and thinking level.
The Codex Astra/Max preset fills those options for inspection before saving.
Choose a new session, a previous conversation or an exact recorded conversation
explicitly. Running sessions retain their saved start configuration. Retained
terminals from older versions remain available in **Task sessions and journal**.

The patch also fixes resource recovery after a private-runtime update, empty
layout strips and the native terminal paste path. Clipboard tests cover both
the keyboard shortcut and the Edit menu. The previously reported full-screen
flash has not been reproduced, so its cause is not claimed as resolved.

## Use another Mac as a workstation

Open **Agents → Workstations** to pair Macs, review a shared session and send
a work order to its existing Agent. Keep the checkout, tools, build files and
Computer Use on the workstation. The controlling Mac displays the session's
output and observed status, including a notice when its process ends.

This first workflow requires an Agent to be started and shared on the host.
Pairing and input handover are explicit. A delivery receipt does not prove the
task succeeded; an Agent that stays running reports its result in chat.
Computer Use needs the workstation's unlocked desktop and its own permissions.
There is no Internet relay or automatic transfer of accounts or source files.

## Set up a lightweight Mac

The bundled **speccify-setup** skill supports “Bitte mach das Setup”, including
before a project is open. It checks existing tools, preserves working accounts
and configuration, and installs only missing prerequisites. Speccify supplies
its own private Python runtime. Development toolchains and build caches belong
on the workstation unless explicitly requested on the work Mac.

## Platform releases

Mac patches can publish independently. Windows patches are prepared only when
requested; minor and major releases prepare both platforms independently.
Downloads and update feeds retain each platform's actual published version.
Mac delivery never waits for an unfinished Windows build.

Agent-to-Agent coordination, enforced privacy isolation and layered model
responses remain 0.12.0 design work. An Agent's Internal/External label alone
does not restrict its provider or account.

See [Agents and sessions](https://speccify.io/app/agents-and-sessions/),
[Screens and resources](https://speccify.io/app/screens-and-resources/) and
[Workstations](https://speccify.io/app/voice-and-remote/#work-from-a-lightweight-mac).

Use **Environment → Updates** or the
[download page](https://speccify.io/download/) to install the Mac patch.
